boundary_effect.game_extensions: These games retain adapter refresh, rules ticking, fullscreen entry, and cleanup behavior after the guarded delta.
boundary_effect.interface_consequence: The loop interface accepts raw frame time and invokes a game callback with a bounded delta.
boundary_effect.shared_core: The shared scheduler owns the 50 millisecond maximum-delta guard before dispatch.

per_game_summaries.summary: Babel Architect clamps each requestAnimationFrame delta to 50 ms before updating its rules adapter.
Rune Forge Chamber applies a 50 millisecond delta cap before its playing-state rules tick.
Spellweavers Run caps each active animation-frame delta at 50 milliseconds before ticking game state.

similarities.statement: Babel Architect, Rune Forge Chamber, and Spellweavers Run cap each active frame delta at 50 milliseconds before a game-owned update.

boundary_effect.game_extensions: Village Guardian supplies its model tick, while Wizard vs Zombie retains juice diffing, camera effects, and terminal transition logic.
boundary_effect.interface_consequence: The callback boundary exposes only capped elapsed time and leaves rendering side effects to the consumer.
boundary_effect.shared_core: The reusable frame driver owns delta measurement and the 50 millisecond ceiling.

per_game_summaries.summary: Village Guardian clamps requestAnimationFrame delta to 50 before calling its playing-model tick.
Wizard vs Zombie clamps active requestAnimationFrame dt at 50 ms before loop-owned effects and transitions.

similarities.statement: Village Guardian and Wizard vs Zombie also cap requestAnimationFrame delta at 50 milliseconds before loop-owned state work.

boundary_effect.game_extensions: Each game retains its accuracy and XP calculation plus its terminal-to-ended phase transition.
boundary_effect.interface_consequence: The emitter accepts a terminal result and host callback, returning whether that result was newly reported.
boundary_effect.shared_core: The shared completion gate owns the reported latch and suppresses repeat emission for one terminal result.

per_game_summaries.summary: Abyssal Well uses hasReportedRef to emit one host completion after victory or defeat results exist.
Village Guardian marks its ended result reported before invoking the completion callback.
Storm Castle Tower separates terminal result creation from a single ended-result completion effect.

similarities.statement: Abyssal Well, Village Guardian, and Storm Castle Tower latch terminal results before invoking host completion once.

boundary_effect.game_extensions: The cartridge chooses model completion, Sorcerer Ziggurat also guards diagnostics, and Enchanted Library stores UI results.
boundary_effect.interface_consequence: The contract accepts completion readiness and one or more callbacks behind a single-use latch.
boundary_effect.shared_core: The common emitter owns one-time delivery once a model or result is terminal.

per_game_summaries.summary: Griffin Riders Escape delivers completion once after the cartridge model becomes complete.
Sorcerer Ziggurat protects both host and diagnostic completion callbacks with one local latch.
Enchanted Library invokes its host completion at most once after victory or gameover results are stored.

similarities.statement: Griffin Riders Escape, Sorcerer Ziggurat, and Enchanted Library expose a fire-once boundary after model completion.

boundary_effect.game_extensions: Rune Forge Chamber retains fullscreen exit and defeat XP, while Babel Architect retains summary construction and estimated XP.
boundary_effect.interface_consequence: The bridge consumes a terminal outcome and game-built result, then performs one host report alongside game-owned UI effects.
boundary_effect.shared_core: The reusable terminal bridge owns the one-report invariant during a rules-to-UI transition.

per_game_summaries.summary: Rune Forge Chamber reports completion once while moving a rules defeat into ended UI.
Babel Architect enters ended UI and reports one completion summary after either terminal outcome.

similarities.statement: Rune Forge Chamber and Babel Architect report one result while converting a terminal rules outcome into ended UI.

boundary_effect.game_extensions: Each game retains its error wording and the sentence or vocabulary transformation that follows validation.
boundary_effect.interface_consequence: State factories receive a validated nonempty content collection or return a structured construction failure.
boundary_effect.shared_core: The shared constructor guard owns the nonempty collection assertion before any random selection or entity creation.

per_game_summaries.summary: Abyssal Well rejects empty sentence input before selecting or splitting playable content.
Village Guardian throws a named validation error when vocabulary is empty.
Archers Revenge rejects empty vocabulary at state creation.

similarities.statement: Abyssal Well, Village Guardian, and Archers Revenge reject empty playable content before state construction.

boundary_effect.game_extensions: Sentence splitting, seeded graph construction, and vocabulary-progress initialization remain game extensions.
boundary_effect.interface_consequence: The initializer boundary separates content validation from the game-specific target-building callback.
boundary_effect.shared_core: The shared entry guard owns rejection of empty collections, including blank sentence content where supplied.

per_game_summaries.summary: Griffin Riders Escape rejects empty vocabulary before choosing and splitting a sentence.
Sorcerer Ziggurat rejects both absent and blank sentence content before graph construction.
Enchanted Library rejects empty vocabulary before progress and target initialization.

similarities.statement: Griffin Riders Escape, Sorcerer Ziggurat, and Enchanted Library validate nonblank content before target initialization.

boundary_effect.game_extensions: Shuffling, rune-circle generation, and stable seeded target creation remain consumer-owned setup.
boundary_effect.interface_consequence: The setup contract yields validated learning entries before invoking a game-specific deterministic initializer.
boundary_effect.shared_core: The common validation core owns the playable-content presence check, including blank term and translation rejection.

per_game_summaries.summary: Rune Match rejects empty vocabulary before shuffling its active word pool.
Rune Forge Chamber rejects empty vocabulary before sentence selection and circle creation.
Astral Mage rejects absent inputs plus blank terms or translations before deterministic target creation.

similarities.statement: Rune Match, Rune Forge Chamber, and Astral Mage reject empty or blank learning inputs before deterministic setup.

boundary_effect.game_extensions: Circle selection, four-way movement with collect, and three-lane movement remain game-defined action vocabularies.
boundary_effect.interface_consequence: Adapters emit semantic actions without exposing DOM, Phaser, keyboard, or pointer event objects to rules code.
boundary_effect.shared_core: The shared input layer owns deduplication of equivalent click, tap, key, and normalized-region events into action identifiers.

similarities.dimension: physical input to semantic action mapping

per_game_summaries.summary: Rune Forge Chamber maps click and tap activation to one circle-selection action.
Storm Castle Tower maps paired keyboard keys and normalized pointer regions to movement and collect actions.
Spellweavers Run maps alternate arrow and letter keys to the same three lane actions while active.

similarities.statement: Rune Forge Chamber, Storm Castle Tower, and Spellweavers Run map multiple physical events to bounded semantic actions.

boundary_effect.game_extensions: Binary gate choice, swipe thresholds, and isometric left-forward-right movement remain game extensions.
boundary_effect.interface_consequence: The rules-facing interface consumes traversal actions while modality thresholds and bindings stay in adapters.
boundary_effect.shared_core: The common control adapter owns alternate-key and gesture-to-direction normalization.

similarities.dimension: physical input to semantic action mapping

per_game_summaries.summary: Dragon Rider exposes the same left and right choices through paired keys and pointer buttons.
Griffin Riders Escape normalizes paired keys, pointer regions, and swipe gestures into traversal actions.
Sorcerer Ziggurat maps touch controls and paired keyboard keys to three directional steps.

similarities.statement: Dragon Rider, Griffin Riders Escape, and Sorcerer Ziggurat normalize keyboard and touch or pointer controls into traversal choices.

boundary_effect.game_extensions: Enchanted Library retains cast truthiness, while Astral Mage retains Space and pointer FIRE bindings.
boundary_effect.interface_consequence: The boundary exposes a small directional-action snapshot independent of the originating control surface.
boundary_effect.shared_core: The reusable adapter owns conversion from signed axes and discrete physical controls to movement plus ability actions.

similarities.dimension: physical input to semantic action mapping

per_game_summaries.summary: Enchanted Library converts directional adapter values and cast truthiness into semantic input flags.
Astral Mage binds paired movement keys and pointer controls to movement and fire actions.

similarities.statement: Enchanted Library and Astral Mage convert directional and fire or cast controls into rules-facing action flags.

boundary_effect.game_extensions: Rune Forge Chamber supplies health and rotating-level behavior, while Babel Architect supplies stability decay and its clamp.
boundary_effect.interface_consequence: The evaluator accepts a time predicate and a game-owned terminal predicate, returning one terminal reason without merging resources.
boundary_effect.shared_core: The shared threshold evaluator can own elapsed-time expiry without owning the secondary resource predicate.

per_game_summaries.summary: Rune Forge Chamber decrements active time and defeats on time expiry or depleted health.
Babel Architect advances elapsed time and defeats on timeout or zero stability.

differences.statement: Rune Forge Chamber and Babel Architect share timeout termination but couple it to health and stability resources respectively.

boundary_effect.game_extensions: Both dragon games retain their running and boss state vocabulary plus any boss-entry effects.
boundary_effect.interface_consequence: The time interface receives elapsed delta and duration, returning bounded elapsed time with a threshold event.
boundary_effect.shared_core: The shared duration tracker owns monotonic elapsed-time clamping and the single threshold-crossed signal.

per_game_summaries.summary: Dragon Flight clamps elapsed time at its duration and enters boss state at the threshold.
Dragon Rider clamps elapsed time at duration and changes a running state to boss.

similarities.statement: Dragon Flight and Dragon Rider clamp elapsed time at a configured duration and enter boss state when that threshold is reached.

boundary_effect.game_extensions: End-game invocation, defeat return, and mana-or-time gameover policy remain distinct game extensions.
boundary_effect.interface_consequence: The tick contract returns remaining time plus a threshold event that game rules map to their terminal state.
boundary_effect.shared_core: The common countdown core owns nonnegative decrement and detection of the zero boundary during active play.

per_game_summaries.summary: Magic Defense decrements its playing timer once per second and ends the game at zero.
Village Guardian transitions the ticked model to defeat when its decremented timer crosses zero.
Enchanted Library floors remaining time at zero and enters gameover when time or mana is exhausted.

similarities.statement: Magic Defense, Village Guardian, and Enchanted Library transition active play when a countdown reaches zero.

boundary_effect.game_extensions: Trail append, orb removal with combo, and rune health penalties remain game-owned consequences.
boundary_effect.interface_consequence: The interface accepts current target and candidate identity, returning match status and next progress index.
boundary_effect.shared_core: The shared progression core owns current-target comparison and one-step ordered advancement.

per_game_summaries.summary: Village Guardian collects the in-order villager and advances its target index.
Spellweavers Run removes a correct orb, advances target progress, and wins after the final word.
Rune Forge Chamber advances progress only when the selected circle word matches the current target.

similarities.statement: Village Guardian, Spellweavers Run, and Rune Forge Chamber advance ordered progress only after the current target is selected.

boundary_effect.game_extensions: Sentence loading, gate penalties and combo, plus graph-node lighting remain game extensions.
boundary_effect.interface_consequence: The sequencer returns next target position and sequence-complete status to a game-owned transition handler.
boundary_effect.shared_core: The reusable target sequencer owns correct-choice advancement and detection of the sequence boundary.

per_game_summaries.summary: Storm Castle Tower advances a correct target and finishes or loads the next sentence at its boundary.
Griffin Riders Escape advances collected words and target index for a correct gate.
Sorcerer Ziggurat advances token and graph-node progress after a legal correct step.

similarities.statement: Storm Castle Tower, Griffin Riders Escape, and Sorcerer Ziggurat advance ordered targets after a correct spatial choice.

boundary_effect.game_extensions: Trail scattering, mastery and shield rewards, and cauldron warning or completion behavior stay game-specific.
boundary_effect.interface_consequence: The contract returns correct or incorrect plus an updated progress token while extensions apply spatial and resource effects.
boundary_effect.shared_core: The shared matcher owns expected-content comparison and successful progress mutation.

per_game_summaries.summary: Dungeon Liberator appends an in-order prisoner to the progress trail while scattering out-of-order contact.
Enchanted Library advances the selected word's mastery progress after a correct book collision.
Potion Rush starts on the indexed first word and advances only exact next ingredients in sequence.

similarities.statement: Dungeon Liberator, Enchanted Library, and Potion Rush record progress only for the expected ordered content interaction.

boundary_effect.game_extensions: Astral Mage retains wrong-token score deduction, while Babel Architect retains unstable placements and stability loss.
boundary_effect.interface_consequence: The interface requires stable candidate identity rather than visible text alone and returns the advanced position.
boundary_effect.shared_core: The common ordered-target core owns identity-safe matching and advancement of exactly one expected position.

per_game_summaries.summary: Astral Mage advances ordered progress by stable target identity and leaves wrong visible-token hits unadvanced.
Babel Architect advances ordered construction only for the expected block.

similarities.statement: Astral Mage and Babel Architect advance ordered progress only for a stable target identity or expected block.

boundary_effect.game_extensions: Weighted combat efficiency, zero-attempt handling, and configured survival or speed bonuses remain separate formulas.
boundary_effect.interface_consequence: The calculator interface accepts named counters and a game-owned formula policy, returning bounded XP with no UI dependency.
boundary_effect.shared_core: The shared result layer can own validated performance inputs, finite arithmetic, and an explicit XP cap.

per_game_summaries.summary: RPG Battle combines health, turn efficiency, and streak performance into XP clamped from one through ten.
Abyssal Well derives capped XP from attempts, correct words, accuracy, survival, and speed.
Village Guardian caps correct-answer base XP after applying accuracy, speed, and survival bonuses.

differences.statement: RPG Battle, Abyssal Well, and Village Guardian derive capped XP from different combinations of accuracy, efficiency, survival, speed, and streak counters.

boundary_effect.game_extensions: Mana and speed bonuses, floor-of-accuracy multiplication, and reputation or progression bonuses remain game policies.
boundary_effect.interface_consequence: The result function receives normalized counters and an injected policy that declares rounding and cap behavior.
boundary_effect.shared_core: The reusable accounting boundary owns counter validation and deterministic XP result construction.

per_game_summaries.summary: Enchanted Library derives XP from attempts, accuracy, mana, and elapsed-time bonuses with a ten-point cap.
Alchemists Synthesis multiplies correct answers by derived accuracy and floors the XP result.
Potion Rush combines completed sentences with accuracy, reputation, speed, and progression bonuses under a cap.

differences.statement: Enchanted Library, Alchemists Synthesis, and Potion Rush all derive XP from performance but use distinct bonus and cap policies.

boundary_effect.game_extensions: Magic Defense retains multiplicative flooring, while Rune Forge Chamber retains additive bonuses and maxXP.
boundary_effect.interface_consequence: The interface makes rounding, bonus weights, and upper bounds explicit policy inputs rather than hidden shared defaults.
boundary_effect.shared_core: The shared accounting contract owns typed performance counters and integer XP output, not one universal formula.

per_game_summaries.summary: Magic Defense floors the product of correct answers and accuracy to produce XP.
Rune Forge Chamber caps per-word base XP after accuracy, speed, and survival bonuses.

differences.statement: Magic Defense multiplies correct answers by accuracy, while Rune Forge Chamber adds accuracy, speed, and survival bonuses to per-word XP.
